meta.title: Practical AI. Better Leadership.
meta.intro: A living library of useful, free resources for team leaders, aspiring managers, and small-business owners who want practical AI and clearer leadership—not hype.
meta.bio: Practical AI for better leadership. Workflows, prompts, and ideas for team leaders, aspiring managers, and small-business owners.

this_week.title: 4 areas where companies need AI guardrails
this_week.why: Based on interviews with 48 leaders, it argues for putting oversight where it matters most (architecture, experiments, workforce skills, and vendors) instead of building separate rules for every AI tool.

this_week.title: Why Leaders Need to Rethink Their Approach to AI Oversight
this_week.why: When people are slow to adopt AI, more monitoring and mandates can push them to hide their use; this piece explains why trust works better than tighter control.

this_week.title: Your AI Strategy Is Your Middle Managers
this_week.why: Practical take on why managers make or break AI adoption, with a simple green, amber, red way to agree with your team which uses are fine, which need a check, and which need approval.

this_week.title: Three Ways to Work with AI, and How to Choose
this_week.why: Clear framework for centaur, cyborg, and conjurer modes—so you decide how much of a task to keep, share, or hand off before you start prompting.

this_week.title: Manager AI Adoption Playbook: Six-Week Plan
this_week.why: Week-by-week plan to pick one workflow, set safe-use rules, add human checkpoints, and measure quality—not just logins.

this_week.title: AI for Managers: How to Lead a Team That Uses AI
this_week.why: Practical starting workflows (status reports, 1:1 prep, meeting actions) plus a one-page rules outline managers can actually use.

workflows.title: Management as AI Superpower
workflows.why: Why management skills—clear goals, evaluation, and feedback—matter more as AI agents do longer stretches of work.

workflows.title: AI Workflows: A Practical Guide for Project Managers
workflows.why: Defines an AI workflow as trigger → context → model → human review → output, with ownership and privacy called out explicitly.

workflows.title: How to Use AI for Business Automation
workflows.why: Sensible sequence for small teams: map repetitive work, automate one simple flow first, keep humans on customer-facing and high-risk steps.

workflows.title: Business Process Automation (overview)
workflows.why: Plain-language overview of when process automation helps—and when a messy process needs a SOP before a tool.

prompts.title: 1:1 prep brief
prompts.why: Turn scattered notes into a sharp agenda without inventing performance judgments.

prompts.title: Meeting notes → actions
prompts.why: Convert a transcript or rough notes into owners and due dates you can send for confirmation.

prompts.title: Delegation brief for an AI agent
prompts.why: Brief AI the way you would brief a new hire—goal, constraints, definition of done, and checks.

prompts.title: Weekly status from raw updates
prompts.why: Draft a status update for stakeholders while keeping escalation decisions with you.

prompts.title: SOP from a walkthrough
prompts.why: Turn a recorded process into a draft SOP you still approve before it becomes team truth.

prompts.title: Decision memo (options + recommendation)
prompts.why: Force a clear recommendation with assumptions and kill criteria—useful for managers and owners alike.

leadership.title: Want to Become a Better Leader? Question Your Assumptions
leadership.source: Knowledge at Wharton (Adam Grant & Erika James)
leadership.why: Evidence-based reminder to rethink management habits—pairs well with AI experiments where old assumptions fail fast.

leadership.title: Why You Need a Challenge Network
leadership.why: On surrounding yourself with thoughtful skeptics who catch blind spots—especially useful when AI makes weak ideas look polished.

leadership.title: The Shape of the Thing
leadership.why: Big-picture leadership read on the shift from co-intelligence chat to managing agents—and why org choices now set precedents.

smb.title: Business Automation: Transform Your Operations
smb.why: Owner-friendly starting point: audit repetitive work, automate one flow, measure time and errors before expanding.

smb.title: Operations Automation: Everything You Need to Know
smb.why: Practical ops framing for small businesses—what to automate in handoffs between apps without losing accountability.

smb.title: n8n Workflow Templates (open library)
smb.why: Browse free automation templates if you prefer self-hosted or open workflows; always adapt and review before connecting real data.

healthcare.title: Artificial Intelligence for Drug Development
healthcare.why: FDA hub for how AI shows up in drug development submissions—useful for leaders who need a regulatory map before funding pilots that may later support safety, efficacy, or quality decisions.

healthcare.title: Considerations for the Use of Artificial Intelligence To Support Regulatory Decision-Making for Drug and Biological Products
healthcare.why: Draft guidance on risk-based credibility assessment for AI models used in regulatory decisions—start here when defining context of use, documentation, and human oversight for life-sciences AI work.

healthcare.title: Ethics and governance of artificial intelligence for health
healthcare.why: Consensus principles (autonomy, safety, transparency, accountability, equity, sustainability) that still frame governance and privacy conversations for health AI programs.

healthcare.title: Ethics and governance of artificial intelligence for health: Guidance on large multi-modal models
healthcare.why: Practical recommendations for governments, developers, and providers on generative multi-modal models—including risks of inaccurate outputs and the need for post-release audit and data protection.

healthcare.title: Artificial intelligence (EMA overview)
healthcare.why: EU regulator’s page on AI across the medicine lifecycle—helps pharma leaders align internal AI use with European expectations, not only U.S. FDA framing.

healthcare.title: 2026 Life sciences outlook
healthcare.why: Executive survey view of AI scaling, regulation, and cybersecurity pressure in biopharma and medtech—useful for setting realistic adoption goals when few leaders report significant AI returns yet.

healthcare.title: Redesigning leadership for clinical AI deployment
healthcare.why: On leadership structures that actually support clinical AI—clinical champions, multidisciplinary teams, and frontline engagement rather than a single tech rollout plan.

healthcare.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Medical Devices
healthcare.why: Device-side FDA landing page for AI-enabled medical devices—helps healthcare leaders separate SaMD regulatory paths from drug-development AI uses.

healthcare.title: Generative AI in life sciences marketing
healthcare.why: Survey of marketing leaders on gen AI for concept ideation, derivative content, and why MLR process redesign—not just more drafts—is the bottleneck to scale.

healthcare.title: Agentic AI in life sciences commercialization strategy
healthcare.why: Argues commercialization needs decision systems across sales, marketing, and access—not a pile of disconnected AI pilots—with human review still in the loop.

healthcare.title: Medical affairs outlook report 2026: Key trends and insights
healthcare.why: Outlook for medical affairs leaders on where AI and analytics fit scientific engagement and insight work—useful when commercial AI plans need a medical counterpart.

healthcare.title: Reinventing Pharma Customer Engagement with AI
healthcare.why: Field-focused view of AI for call planning, personalized HCP content, and cross-functional collaboration among sales, medical, and market access—with compliance framed as part of the engagement design.

healthcare.title: Reinventing Life Sciences Age of Generative AI
healthcare.why: Commercialization section covers access/contracting, marketing content under regulatory constraints, MLR-assisted review, and field assistants—good overview before picking one workflow to pilot.

healthcare.title: AI in Life Sciences Commercialization
healthcare.why: 2025 survey of commercial leaders on adoption across sales, marketing, market access, and compliance—useful for benchmarking where peers still struggle to industrialize tools.

healthcare.title: Omnichannel Engagement in Pharma: Harnessing the Power of Generative AI
healthcare.why: On next-best-action and gen AI in HCP omnichannel programs—practical for leaders who need to measure engagement quality, not just content volume.

healthcare.title: Best use cases for scaling agentic AI in commercial life sciences
healthcare.why: Checklist mindset for which commercial AI use cases scale (repetitive but reviewable; immediate value for reps) versus experiments that stall—pairs well with adoption and impact measurement.

healthcare.title: The System-Level View That Sound Market Access Decisions Are Missing
healthcare.source: Pharmaceutical Commerce (Matthew Champion and Kunal Akwalia, IQVIA)
healthcare.why: Shows how market access teams can use scenario modeling, including AI agents that rebuild models as inputs change, to see how pricing, coverage, contracting, and affordability choices affect each other before committing.

healthcare.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence for Health Technology Assessment: Opportunities, Challenges, and Policy Considerations
healthcare.why: Working-group view of gen AI in HTA/HEOR—literature review, RWE, and economic modeling—with privacy, bias, and human oversight called out for market-access leaders.

healthcare.title: The Office of Prescription Drug Promotion (OPDP)
healthcare.why: FDA office that oversees prescription-drug promotional communications—baseline context for any marketing-content or MLR AI pilot so teams know what still needs human promotional review.

industry_groups.label: Medical devices & biotech
industry_groups.blurb: Field sales, reimbursement, and commercial leadership in device and biotech companies. Sits next to Healthcare & pharma.

industry_groups.label: Financial services & insurance
industry_groups.blurb: Claims, underwriting, compliance, and advisor productivity in regulated financial firms.

industry_groups.label: Retail & consumer goods
industry_groups.blurb: Store and district managers, forecasting, and customer service.

industry_groups.label: Manufacturing & supply chain
industry_groups.blurb: Plant supervisors, quality, safety, scheduling, and planning.

industry_groups.label: Small business & professional services
industry_groups.blurb: Owners and small firms: marketing, bookkeeping, client follow-up, and getting started safely.

industry_groups.label: Education & nonprofits
industry_groups.blurb: Principals, district leaders, and program leads doing more with less.

industry_groups.label: Sales leadership
industry_groups.blurb: Cross-industry: coaching, call prep, account and territory planning.

industries.title: Scaling gen AI in the medtech industry
industries.why: Survey-backed look at where medtech teams are getting value from gen AI, including CRM-based sales tools, coaching aids for sales managers, and faster content and legal review.

industries.title: Building an effective AI strategy for medtech organizations
industries.why: Argues for starting from the decisions you want to improve, not the tool, and tying each use case to revenue, productivity, or customer-experience goals.

industries.title: Can agentic AI improve workflows and margins in medtech?
industries.why: Walks through where AI agents could help in medtech, from contracting and pricing to field service and commercial content, and where people still need to decide.

industries.title: Three key trends likely to shape medtech in 2026
industries.why: Short read on portfolio shifts, the move to outpatient care, and AI governance. Useful context for commercial leaders planning the year.

industries.title: Tips to Overcome AI Medical Device Reimbursement Woes
industries.why: A founder's lessons on getting coverage, coding, and payment for an AI-enabled device, and why to talk to FDA, CMS, and payers early.

industries.title: The future of AI in the insurance industry
industries.why: How insurers are reworking whole areas like claims, underwriting, and distribution instead of running scattered pilots, and why change management is half the work.

industries.title: How banks can supercharge intelligent automation with agentic AI
industries.why: Where AI agents fit in banking processes such as credit underwriting and fraud work, and why compliance has to be built in from the start.

industries.title: Managing the new wave of risks from AI agents in banking
industries.why: Practical governance ideas for AI agents: named owners, activity logs, escalation triggers, and human review for consequential decisions.

industries.title: GenAI: Continuing and Emerging Trends (2026 FINRA Annual Regulatory Oversight Report)
industries.why: The regulator's view of how existing supervision, communications, and recordkeeping rules apply when firms use gen AI and AI agents. A good compliance checklist.

industries.title: The Insurance CEO’s Blueprint for Scaling AI
industries.why: Lays out six places insurers can build AI once and reuse it, from claims and underwriting to giving sales agents more time with customers, plus a short leadership checklist.

industries.title: The case for agentic AI in retail with AI-sourcing
industries.why: Concrete store examples like shelf monitoring, staff scheduling, and task assignment, plus how merchandising, planning, and customer care could change.

industries.title: Elevating the retail floor: How will AI reshape frontline retail roles and the customer experience?
industries.why: How AI could free up store associates' time and change customer service, and what that means for hiring and training frontline teams.

industries.title: State of AI in retail and CPG
industries.why: A survey of 200 consumer-sector executives that found high conviction but uneven execution. Quick benchmark for where your team stands.

industries.title: 2026 Global Retail Industry Outlook
industries.why: The big-picture outlook for retail leaders, including how AI is moving from pilots into pricing, personalization, and planning.

industries.title: Agentic AI in customer care: What's on leaders' minds?
industries.why: Customer-service leaders on running a hybrid team of people and AI agents: shared metrics, new training, and starting from real customer pain points.

industries.title: From vision to value: A road map for enterprise transformation in manufacturing with agentic AI
industries.why: Shop-floor examples like AI-drafted work instructions reviewed by engineers, plus why most task hours stay human and how to bring workers along.

industries.title: How COOs maximize operational impact from gen AI and agentic AI
industries.why: Includes a maintenance copilot for frontline technicians and an AI-prepared shift handover that the supervisor reviews before acting.

industries.title: 6 steps to succeeding with industrial AI
industries.why: Keep scope small, frame problems clearly, and get timely data to the people on the floor who make real-time decisions.

industries.title: The Future of Supply Chain Planning: Faster, Smarter Decisions with LLMs
industries.why: How planners can ask plain-language what-if questions of their planning tools and get answers in minutes instead of days.

industries.title: Real-life ways small firms use AI
industries.why: Four accounting practices with fewer than 10 people show how they use AI for research, prospect intake, invoice approvals, and client-satisfaction checks, with a human reviewing the work.

industries.title: AI for Small Business 101: How to Get Started
industries.source: CO— by U.S. Chamber of Commerce
industries.why: Beginner-friendly guide to picking AI tools for marketing, customer service, and admin tasks, with tips on trying them safely.

industries.title: AI readiness checklist for SMBs: A practical starting point
industries.why: A five-step check of your data, tools, and processes so you can start small, prove value, and then grow.

industries.title: New Advocacy Article Highlights Small Businesses Closing the AI Adoption Gap
industries.why: Census-based data on how fast small firms are adopting AI. They're ahead in some areas, like automated marketing.

industries.title: AI Use in Schools Is Quickly Increasing but Guidance Lags Behind
industries.why: National surveys of teachers, school and district leaders, students, and parents. Shows how fast AI use is growing and where policy and training lag.

industries.title: Strategies for Taking Advantage of AI as a New Administrator
industries.why: A new administrator shares how they use AI to save time on communications, planning, and data, and where they keep their own judgment.

industries.title: How to Make Purposeful Decisions About Generative AI in Your School
industries.why: Guidance for school leaders writing AI policies: involve teachers, start with clear goals, and revisit the rules as tools change.

industries.title: How AI Can Deepen Nonprofit Relationships
industries.why: How nonprofits can use AI to know donors better and personalize outreach without losing the human relationship.

industries.title: How to Use A.I. Effectively and Protect Your Organization's Reputation and Values
industries.why: Experts explain why nonprofits need written AI-use guidelines and how to draft them.

industries.title: AI Is Transforming Productivity, but Sales Remains a New Frontier
industries.why: Why sales teams lag other functions on AI, and how to start: pick one or two process-ready areas like prospecting, clean the data, and redesign the workflow.

industries.title: Five ways B2B sales leaders can win with tech and AI
industries.why: Covers AI-drafted account plans, lead prioritization, RFP drafts, and call analysis that points coaching at each rep's skill gaps.

industries.title: How Successful Sales Teams Are Embracing Agentic AI
industries.why: What changes when AI agents work alongside reps to find, nurture, and close deals, and what managers should still own.

industries.title: Why Some Sales Teams Are Actually Growing Alongside AI
industries.why: For complex, high-stakes purchases, buyers still want a person who helps them sort through uncertainty. Explains how sales roles are shifting.

videos.title: How AI Is Changing Strategy—and 4 Skills Leaders Need Next
videos.why: Mollick on why treating AI as only a productivity tool backfires—and what leaders should decide urgently.

videos.title: Ethan Mollick on an AI Strategy for Organizations to Succeed
videos.why: Leadership–lab–crowd model for getting AI adoption out of pilots and into real work.

videos.title: Andrew Ng on building AI-native teams | AI Fund Frontier ‘26
videos.why: Concrete leadership moves for AI-native teams: platforms, processes, and empowered high-context groups.

videos.title: AI for Everyone by Andrew Ng
videos.why: Non-technical grounding in what AI can and cannot do—still a solid on-ramp for aspiring managers.

videos.title: Software engineering with LLMs in 2025: reality check (at LDX3 by LeadDev)
videos.why: Practical reality check on LLM workflows from Simon Willison—useful even if you lead non-engineering teams adopting agents.

videos.title: How to Give & Get Constructive Feedback | Dr. Adam Grant & Dr. Andrew Huberman
videos.why: Leadership skill that AI cannot replace: giving and receiving feedback without ego theater.

videos.title: How to Change Your Workplace | WorkLife with Adam Grant
videos.why: On diagnosing what is actually broken before you roll out the next change—including AI tools.

videos.title: Brené Brown and Simon Sinek on the leadership skills we need to build | Re:Thinking with Adam Grant
videos.why: Conversation on learnable leadership skills—useful balance beside the AI workflow content.

videos.title: REdI 2024 | D2S05 - Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning: The New Frontier of Drug Development..
videos.why: FDA staff walk through AI/ML in drug development submissions and a risk-based credibility mindset—good orientation for pharma leaders before drafting internal AI rules.

videos.title: How pharma can redesign decision-making to unlock AI value | Aaron Mitchell, ZS
videos.why: ZS commercial perspective on redesigning decisions—not just tooling—so AI adoption sticks in pharma organizations.

archive.title: Agency and Agents
archive.why: On when agents should pull humans in—for approval, expertise, exceptions, and interesting decisions—so you do not automate the wrong half of the job.

archive.title: The Four Ps — How to Manage an AI-Native Engineering Team
archive.why: A leadership checklist around People, Projects, Platforms, and Processes. Useful even if you do not manage engineers—same pattern applies to any knowledge team adopting AI.

archive.title: How AI Is Changing Strategy (podcast with Ethan Mollick)
archive.why: Short listen on why AI is a strategy question, not just a productivity add-on, and why managers should experiment instead of waiting for a perfect playbook.

archive.title: The looming advisor shortage in US wealth management
archive.why: Sizes the coming advisor gap and shows where gen AI can give advisors time back: meeting prep, notes, plan drafts, and compliance tasks.
